sections.title: Architecture Spine
sections.content: Evidence-gated artifact DAG: Acceptance owns closure, checks, routing, import, and finalization; Bootstrap produces non-authorizing evidence. Immutable complete identities, canonical evidence primitives, full-source delivery or controller-owned projections, stable segment descriptors, real required checks, event-based recovery, and typed routes fail closed on mismatch or staleness.

sections.title: Specification
sections.content: CAP-1 through CAP-10 require identity-bound acceptance inputs, complete consumer closure, deterministic checks before model work, isolated three-role Bootstrap review where required, bounded recovery, cost decisions, exact evidence import, and semantic regression coverage. Lifecycle owners remain separated; assistant or advisory text is never authority.

sections.title: Authority and Lifecycle
sections.content: VDD owns draft/plan-ready, maintainer owns implementation-authorized and non-authorizing supervised decisions, Quick Dev owns implementation-complete, and Acceptance alone publishes acceptance-passed. Mode and route are orthogonal; triggers force full review or pause.

sections.title: Projection and Segmentation
sections.content: Selected authority is delivered completely within budget; over-budget content uses immutable hash-bound range projections. Segment assignments, requests, receipts, folds, and retries share one canonical descriptor. Children receive only frozen assigned snapshots and inherited access proof.

sections.title: Execution and Recovery
sections.content: Append-only process events govern attempts. Heartbeats prove liveness only; controller-validated effective progress refreshes no-progress windows. Terminal events, process identity, leases, retries, and recovery are policy-bound and non-authorizing on failure.

sections.title: Verification and Rollout
sections.content: Cost decisions precede launch. Regression and frozen semantic corpus must prove no omission, false authorization, transport-as-semantics, boundary escape, stale lease, or route downgrade. Delivery proceeds M0 recovery/isolation, M1 Acceptance strategy, then M2 scale and finalization.

sections.title: Diagrams and Glossary
sections.content: Diagrams depict lifecycle routing and attempt reconciliation. Glossary defines Acceptance, Bootstrap Complete Review, closure, required checks, projections, segment snapshots, process events, modes, routes, and non-authorizing results.

sections.title: Memory Log
sections.content: Historical process record confirms the canonical package, adopted architecture, resolved range/runtime/vcec-r1n decisions, and remaining policy measurement questions. It reinforces that authoritative implementation obligations are the finalized specification and companions.
